verdict.line: You lose if you fight into a full Q-stack shockwave at your tower; you win if you force trades before level 6 and punish Path Maker's dash commitment.

brief.thesis: Both champions are built to all-in, but K'Sante's E (Footwork) and shield uptime let him disengage your Q/W combo for free, while your R (World Ender) is the one tool that outlasts his R (All Out) cooldown-for-cooldown. The data backs this as genuinely close — 52.7% over 2810 games — because the lane is won on who commits to the all-in with cooldowns up, not raw stats.

theirWindow.when: he has 2 Ntofo Strikes stacks up
theirWindow.what: The second Q stack fires a shockwave that pulls you in — do not sit in minion-wave range when he's landed one Q already, since the second hit chains into a stun-adjacent pull you can't Flash out of mid-animation.

yourWindow.when: his W (Path Maker) is on cooldown (14-10s)
yourWindow.what: Path Maker's charge-up gives him reduced damage only while charging; once he dashes, the stun/knockback is spent for 10-14 seconds. Walk him down with E (Umbral Dash) resets and stack Q swings — he has no disengage besides E (Footwork) shield-dash, which doesn't stop your auto-heal.

powerCurve.note: Trade Q pokes, avoid his Q-stack shockwave range
W (Path Maker) stun window opens up kills
R (World Ender) sustain matches his all-in
Black Cleaver stacks shred his armor fast

start.why: 53.8% win rate over 2224 games; the lifesteal and AD pad your trades against his Q poke before he hits his stack threshold.

boots.why: 53.1% over 2022 games; K'Sante's Q autos and empowered All Out attacks are physical, so the flat reduction cuts his poke and his all-in burst.

core.why: Stacks from Q (The Darkin Blade) swings shred his armor, which matters since K'Sante stacks resistances passively — this is your answer to his tankiness.
The on-hit proc rewards landing Q swings in extended trades and gives you a shield to match his Footwork shield.
Converts his burst into damage-over-time you can heal through with E (Umbral Dash) and R lifesteal, which is critical since his All Out burst window is short but heavy.

situational.when: the game goes long and you're resetting R (World Ender) multiple times per fight
you're ahead and want to close out all-ins before his shield (E, Footwork) comes off cooldown
he's building full tank and you need the HP buffer to survive his W (Path Maker) stun chain

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain stacking directly counters his shield-based poke-and-reset pattern, and it scales into extended trades where he has to commit E (Footwork) just to survive.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport sits at 51.3% over 40.5% pick rate; Teleport lets you reset after all-in attempts and still join the rest of the map, since this lane doesn't snowball hard enough to justify forcing Ignite kill pressure.

playing.title: Count his Q stacks before engaging
playing.detail: Q (Ntofo Strikes) has a 3.5s cooldown and builds stacks on hit — at 2 stacks he fires a pulling shockwave. Never walk into melee range when he's already landed one Q in the exchange.

playing.title: Punish Path Maker's charge animation
playing.detail: W (Path Maker) telegraphs with a charge-up before the dash-stun. If you see the charge start, disengage with E (Umbral Dash) rather than trading through it — eating the stun chains directly into his burst.

playing.title: Track his E (Footwork) shield for all-in timing
playing.detail: Footwork's cooldown is 10-8s and grants a shield on use. If he's just spent it to poke or reposition, that's your window to commit Q-W-E without him having a disengage tool up.

playing.title: Save R (World Ender) to outlast All Out
playing.detail: His R (All Out) is 120-80s and trades his defenses for damage — a short, high-risk window. Your R has matching cooldown but gives sustained healing and AD, so popping it in response to his All Out often wins the extended fight.

playing.title: Use Q's three-swing reset to zone, not all-in
playing.detail: Q (The Darkin Blade) has three different swing AoEs on a 14-6s cooldown. Use the first two swings to poke and control space pre-6; save the third swing reset for when you're actually committing to a kill.

playing.title: Black Cleaver stacks win extended trades
playing.detail: Since he stacks resistances through All Out and passive tankiness, prioritize landing every Q swing in a trade to stack Cleaver fast — this is how you turn an even fight into a won one by level 11-15.

playing.title: Don't force all-ins through his stun
playing.detail: If his W (Path Maker) and R (All Out) are both up, do not initiate — the stun-into-burst combo is where most Aatrox deaths in this matchup come from. Wait for one of the two to be spent.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures come from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the tactical reading of cooldown windows and stack timing is my own analysis layered on top.
